newsitem.title: GREECE: UPDATE: STRIKES SWEEP GREECE, FARMERS CUT NATIONAL ROAD.
newsitem.headline: UPDATE: STRIKES SWEEP GREECE, FARMERS CUT NATIONAL ROAD.

text.p: Greek workers crippled transport, schools, hospitals and public services with a 24-hour strike on Thursday and farmers cut the main north-south highway to protest against the ruling socialists' new austerity budget.

Government and union officials said the strike disrupted air, sea, train and urban transport. No buses or trolleys and only a few taxis appeared in Athens. Ministries were working with reduced staffs.

The General Confederation of Greek Workers (GSEE), the largest public and private sector grouping, said the strike was followed by 70 to 100 percent of its members in its various federations. Government officials put the figure lower and said there was little sign of private sector workers joining in.
Farmers, demanding higher price supports and fuel susidies, blocked the main north-south national road with 2,000 tractors, halting traffic between the capital and Greece's second city of Salonika.
The farmers' road blockade was gaining momentum and farmer representatives said they might extend the road blocks through Friday.
The strike was called to protest against the 1997 austerity budget, due to be presented on Friday.
National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou has said the budget will be the toughest in 15 years as Greece struggles to get its economy in line with its European Union partners.
Papandoniou and Prime Minister Costas Simitis have said that their priority was joining European economic and monetary union (EMU) by 2001, two years after a main block of EU states is due to do so.
Papandoniou has vowed to tax the wealthy hard but he has rejected numerous requests from organised labour to ease the economic hardship of lower salaried workers.
"This governement feels for the problems of the workers, and especially the weaker social strata and asks for understanding," a government statement said on Thursday.
But it said following the austerity plan and maintaining a strong drachma policy to fight inflation were the best ways to support the real income of wage earners, pensioners and farmers.
"The new taxes in the 1997 budget will fall exclusively on higher incomes," it said.
GSEE, with some three million members, called the strike and the union of civil servants (ADEDY) joined in.
"GSEE expresses its full rejection of the announced economic austerity policy and will fight for protection and improvement of the income of workers and pensioners," a statement said.

Workers at state-run Olympic Airways staged a three-hour stoppage in the morning, delaying international and domestic flights. Civil aviation employees, except traffic controllers, have called for a three-hour stoppage in the evening.

Some 8,000 to 10,000 GSEE and ADEDY workers marched through Athens to the national economy ministry to demand the budget be amended before being voted in parliament in December. Similar marches were held in other main cities, including Salonika and Patras -- a western port city. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
